script.opening_words: The most expensive thing that happened on February 28th, 2026 won't show up on most people's bank statements until October, maybe November. And by then, most people will have completely forgotten what caused it. That's not a metaphor. That's the actual timeline. What started as a military strike on Iran has set off five separate economic shocks moving toward your wallet on five different timelines, each one bigger than the last, each one disguised as something completely unrelated by the
script.ending_words: slightly earlier than everyone else and doing five boring, unglamorous things while the rest of the world was still filing it under annoying but manageable. Most people will spend the rest of 2026 confused about why everything keeps getting more expensive. You just spent 20 minutes understanding exactly why. The only question is whether that understanding turns into action or just into a really informed complaint at the dinner table.
script.analysis: Full 17680 canonical characters read. A news-driven explainer: delayed-cost hook, timeline of the 28 February 2026 strikes and Hormuz closure, IEA response and oil prices, two composite households (Maya; Ryan and Jess), five waves (gas, groceries, fertilizer, airfare, interest rates), an investor-behaviour section (DALBAR, best days), five actions (emergency fund in high-yield savings, attack card debt, keep investing, book flights, audit energy exposure), two scenarios and a close. Verified: IEA record 400M barrel release and "largest disruption", Brent ~$120 peak, late-March gas/diesel levels, Fed hold at 3.50-3.75%, $1.28T card debt, DALBAR 848 bp/15 years, urea +~50% and Hormuz third of urea trade, jet fuel ~+58% week. Wrong or unsupported: 5.87% February mortgage baseline (Freddie 5.98%), "32% in a single week" NOLA, Spirit 124%, 15,000% vs 91%, "1973 and 1979 combined". Attribution problem: DALBAR research described as "our research". The Maya grocery example (+12-21%) overstates the 4.4% CPI projection. The stored ending is complete.
